title: US Energy Chief Exhorts Data Center Backers to Push Back Against Opponents
source_used: Reuters report of 30 Jun 2026, read as the Hawaii Tribune-Herald copy of 1 Jul 2026
key_facts: US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said on Tuesday 30 Jun 2026, at an Amazon Web Services conference, that supporters of data centres should push back against critics, calling concerns about the facilities 'overblown' (Reuters).
He listed opponents' concerns about water and power use, job losses from AI and harm to communities, and said 'right now in the polls, they are winning'.
Wright, a former chief executive of oilfield services company Liberty Energy, likened the issue to opposition to fracking.
A Reuters/Ipsos poll that month showed only one in three Americans approve of the fast pace of data-centre construction.
Wright said 'We'll roll over the opposition to data centers faster than we otherwise should'.
EnergyNow.com shows the same headline dated 16 Oct 2026 (its link path is /2026/06/), so the item is older news republished.
quote_evidence: U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright on Tuesday urged supporters of data centers at an Amazon Web Services conference to push back against critics, saying concerns about the facilities are “overblown.”
Wright, a former CEO of oilfield service company Liberty Energy, likened the issue to opposition he faced over the drilling technique for oil and gas known as fracking.

A Reuters/Ipsos poll this month showed that only one in three Americans approve of the fast pace of data center construction, an issue on the minds of voters and political campaigns ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.
why_it_matters_hint: A cabinet secretary openly told data-centre backers to fight local opposition, but this was said in June.
event_date: 30 Jun 2026 (Wright's speech); EnergyNow republished it dated 16 Oct 2026
